comments.body:
# RCA — CONFIRMED root cause (Phase 1 complete, hypothesis-driven, replicated)

## Verdict in one line

**Gerrit never fails.** All 14 slow `git-upload-pack` requests in the retained log returned
**HTTP 200**. The 504 is manufactured entirely at the edge: nginx's Gerrit `location /` has
**no `proxy_read_timeout`**, so it runs on the compiled-in **60 s** default, while a legitimate
CI change-ref fetch on this host currently takes a **median 36 s / p90 92 s / max 144 s**.
The 60 s ceiling sits *inside* the normal duration distribution, so ~1/3 of CI fetches are
killed mid-flight and reported to the client as a server error.

## The proximate defect (the changeable artifact)

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` — the Gerrit catch-all block:

```nginx
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;      # <- no proxy_read_timeout => nginx default 60s
```

Every **other** proxied location in the same file sets one explicitly
(`proxy_read_timeout 3600s;` at lines 207 / 223 / 246, the three `/mcp` blocks). The location
serving the *longest* operations on the box — git pack generation — is the only one left on the
default. Confirmed on the live host: `grep proxy_read_timeout /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf`
returns exactly three hits, all `3600s`, all `/mcp`.

## Proof

**1. The timeout is nginx's, and it is exactly 60 s.**
CI run 33995047786: fetch issued `22:08:58.46`, 504 returned `22:09:58.73` = **60.27 s**.
Ticket `1e24-bfc0` independently recorded `duration_ms=61003`. My replication measured 60.8 s.

**2. Every timed-out request SUCCEEDED at Gerrit.** From `/var/gerrit/logs/httpd_log`, the four
incident fetches:

| client | start | Gerrit result | Gerrit duration | nginx |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 145.132.103.177 | 22:08:58.72 | **200**, 131070 B | **85.3 s** | 504 at 60 s |
| 172.182.195.43 | 22:08:52.22 | **200**, 131070 B | **91.8 s** | 504 at 60 s |
| 64.236.160.194 | 15:39:25.22 | **200**, 98318 B | **92.4 s** | 504 at 60 s |
| 20.168.98.41 | 15:39:33.41 | **200**, 98318 B | **93.6 s** | 504 at 60 s |

Across the whole retained log: **353 upload-pack POSTs; 14 exceeded 60 s; all 14 returned 200.**
The nginx access log records those same responses as `504 167` — 167 bytes is nginx's own error
page. nginx discarded a successful upstream response and substituted an error.

**3. Rate, predicted then replicated.** Anonymous (CI) substantive fetches: n=37, median 36.0 s,
p90 92.4 s, max 143.9 s, **12/37 = 32.4 % over 60 s**. Authenticated review-bot fetches are much
cheaper (median 12.1 s, 1.6 % over). I then ran the *exact* CI command
(`git fetch https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/84/2684/2`) six times from the
host:

```
iter=1 rc=0   74.7s      iter=4 rc=0   88.7s
iter=2 rc=0   80.1s      iter=5 rc=128 60.8s  HTTP 504
iter=3 rc=0   85.0s      iter=6 rc=128 68.1s  HTTP 504
```

**2/6 = 33 % — matching the 32.4 % predicted from the log.** The bug is reproducible on demand.

**4. Why it is intermittent — and why some fetches survive past 90 s.**
`proxy_read_timeout` is a **gap** timeout, not a total. Iterations 1-4 exceeded 60 s *in total*
and still succeeded, because Gerrit kept emitting bytes. A 504 needs one **silent phase**
(negotiation + `preparePack` counting/delta-compression, which produces no output) to exceed 60 s
on its own. That phase's length is a draw from a distribution whose median sits near the ceiling,
so the same fetch fails and then succeeds seconds later. This is also why all
**78/78** nginx timeouts are `while reading response header from upstream` and **zero** are
body-phase: the failure can only occur before the first byte.

## Why the wall time is high (the contributing capacity condition — quantified)

The host is a **burstable `t4g.large` (2 vCPU / 7.8 GiB)**. CloudWatch:

- `CPUCreditBalance` fell steadily through 2026-09-04 and hit **0.0 at 12:38 UTC on 2026-09-05**,
  and has stayed 0.0 for the following 10 hours.
- `CPUSurplusCreditBalance` has climbed continuously since: **15.5 -> 316.7**.
- `CPUUtilization` sustained **55-74 %** against a **30 % baseline** for t4g.large.

**All four incident 504s (15:38, 15:39, 21:52, 22:08 UTC) occurred after the credit balance hit
zero.** The earlier 02:51-03:08 UTC cluster occurred while it was collapsing (74.9 -> 31.6 -> 13.7).
Consistent with this, upload-pack burns only ~24 % of its wall time on CPU (median across 37 CI
fetches) — it is off-CPU ~76 % of the time; `vmstat` showed `steal` at 13 % and load average
9-12 on 2 vCPU. A full clone needs ~20-28 s of CPU and takes 85-144 s of wall.

Memory is also tight: `rebar-mcp` holds **4.45 GB RSS (55.6 % of RAM)** at 47 % CPU, squeezing the
page cache to ~600 MB on a git server.

## REFUTED — the ticket's own leading hypothesis

**The gate-scratch / root-filesystem IO story is NOT the pathway.** I set out to confirm it and
could not:

- Gerrit's git data is on a **separate EBS device**: `nvme1n1` carries
  `/var/lib/docker/volumes/gerrit_git/_data` and `/var/gerrit`. `gate-scratch` is on
  `nvme0n1p1` (root). Gerrit's packfile reads never touch the contended filesystem.
- `iowait` was 17-18 % then fell to ~1 % while fetches remained slow. The dominant off-CPU
  component tracks **CPU-credit exhaustion and runqueue depth**, not disk.

This is a **CPU/credit** capacity finding, not an IO one. `renowned-corked-hapuku` and
`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` remain real, but they are **not** the mechanism behind these 504s.
The three-ticket unification was attractive and is wrong.

## Also refuted

- **Jetty thread-pool exhaustion** (`httpd.maxThreads = 8`): refuted — every request is serviced
  and returns 200, and the *slowest* requests ran at concurrency **0-1**, while requests at
  concurrency 4-7 completed in 16-24 s. Concurrency is not the driver.
- **JVM GC pause**: refuted — requests complete normally with a uniform ~24 % CPU/wall ratio
  across 37 samples; a GC stall would not produce that, nor 100 % success.
- **Slow ref advertisement**: refuted — `GET .../info/refs` completes in 4-31 ms in every sample.

## AC3 — the distinction the ticket asked for

**Both branches are live, and they are not equal.**

1. **The proxy timeout is genuinely too short for legitimate packfile work.** Gerrit completes
   100 % of these requests successfully. Raising it is a **fix, not a workaround** — it stops the
   edge inventing a failure out of a success. This is the primary defect.
2. **The host also cannot serve in reasonable time**, and that is a separate **capacity** finding
   with a different remedy (credits/instance-class/tenancy), quantified above. Fixing only #2
   still leaves a 60 s ceiling under a distribution that will re-cross it as the repo grows.

## Defect origin (attribution)

The omission dates from **`6cd6f4e1f7c0`** ("S2 (786b): deploy Gerrit + review-bot receiver behind
nginx/TLS", 2026-06-29) — ticket **`786b-190d-5e3a-4194` / `smelly-pane-bolt`**. That commit
created the Gerrit `location /` with `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;` and no timeout, and it has
never had one.

This is an **omission / scope-of-work attribution**, not a regression: no commit made the behaviour
wrong. It became wrong when clone wall-time crossed 60 s under host capacity pressure, so the
appropriate close class is **`preexisting`**, not `regression`.

**The `caused_by` link is NOT recorded.** `rebar link ... caused_by` refuses the target
(`786b` has no commit carrying its trailer) and offers only `--force`. Agents are prohibited from
force overrides, so this is escalated rather than bypassed: an operator should either record
`caused_by` with a scope-of-work reason, or accept the attribution as documented here.

## What I did NOT establish

- I did not measure the *split* between the negotiation phase and `preparePack` inside the silent
  window, so "which sub-phase blows the 60 s" is inferred from the header-phase signature, not
  directly instrumented.
- I did not establish that `rebar-mcp`'s 4.45 GB RSS is a leak rather than steady-state, nor that
  it is the *cause* of credit exhaustion (it is the largest single consumer; that is correlation).
- I did not test the fix. No timeout value has been validated against a real workload.
- I did not establish the autodeploy trigger claimed in `1e24-bfc0`; my incidents do not need it.
  Autodeploy is plausibly one of several things that push an already-credit-starved box over the
  line, but it is not necessary to explain these four failures.

comments.body:
## AC4 belongs to a family — noting it before it gets lost

AC4 ("CI distinguishes a transport failure from a test verdict") is **deferred to a separate change
after the timeout fix lands**, per the coordinator. Recording the shape here so whoever picks it up
does not solve it three times.

Three open tickets are the **same defect class**: *"could not determine" presented as "determined
the bad outcome."*

| ticket | surface | what it cannot distinguish |
|---|---|---|
| `antihuman-beefwitted-zebra` (`5bba`) AC4 | Gerrit Verified Gate checkout | a 504 transport failure vs. the change being broken |
| `deistic-conventual-blackmamba` (`d1d4-8c8b`) | CI vote bot | a superseded/cancelled run vs. a genuine `FAILURE` |
| `erratic-sunny-genet` (`1e28-1322`) | Mirror Guard | "could not reach the host" vs. `healthy:false` |

In each, an **absence of evidence** is rendered as **evidence of a negative**, and the cost is the
same: a `Verified -1` (or an ALARM) that sends good work back around the loop and trains people to
retry. Tonight's four 504s each produced a `Verified -1` on a change whose content never ran.

A single remedy may cover more than one — a shared "indeterminate / infrastructure" outcome that is
neither pass nor fail, and which the voter maps to *no vote* rather than to `-1`. Whoever takes AC4
should scope all three before designing, rather than patching the checkout step alone.

Linked `relates_to` both.

comments.body:
## Sibling sweep (Step 7) — construct and parity axes

**Construct: "a proxied nginx location with no explicit `proxy_read_timeout`."** Two other
locations in `rebar.conf.template` share it — `/review/` and `/opcert/`. Both were checked against
the host's nginx logs rather than changed on suspicion.

**Parity census of every 504 nginx has served (full retained access log):**

```
  32  Gerrit git  (git-upload-pack / info/refs)   <- this bug
 ~11  Gerrit REST (/a/changes/...)                <- SAME location block; also fixed
   2  /mcp                                        <- has an explicit 3600s; different cause
   0  /review/
   0  /opcert/
```

Two useful consequences:

1. **The fix's blast radius is wider than the reported symptom, and correctly so.** The Gerrit
   REST 504s (`/a/changes/<n>/detail?o=LABELS`, the change-status polls the voter and tooling
   make) and the Gerrit UI's static assets (`/elements/gr-app.js` 237 upstream timeouts,
   `/fonts/material-icons.woff2` 207) sit in the *same* `location /` block and were failing for
   the *same* reason. One directive covers all of them. This is very likely a contributor to the
   `voter_errors` climb noted on `ergophobic-harassed-peacock`.

2. **`/review/` and `/opcert/` are NOT confirmed siblings — no speculative change made.**
   `/review/health` does show 254 upstream-timeout lines in the error log, but produced **zero**
   504s, so those are a different class (connect-side, most likely the container being down across
   a redeploy) and belong to `erratic-sunny-genet` / review-bot ops rather than here. `/opcert/`
   shows nothing at all. Neither has a measured duration distribution that would justify a value,
   and inventing one would be the plausibility-driven fix this investigation exists to avoid.
   **Disposition: left unchanged, recorded here.**

3. **`/mcp`'s 2 504s are not this construct** — it already carries an explicit `3600s`, so a
   missing timeout cannot be the cause. That is `witted-invisible-roan` (`9ea3-7d07`), separately
   tracked.

**Push path is covered too.** One of the timeouts was
`GET /a/rebar/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack` — a *push's* ref advertisement. It is a response
read, so it sits under the same `proxy_read_timeout` and is fixed by the same directive.
`proxy_send_timeout` (request-body upload, the other half of a push) is still on its 60s default;
no evidence of it firing was found, so it is left alone rather than changed pre-emptively.

## Summary

Gerrit intermittently fails to serve git fetches, returning **HTTP 504** and killing CI checkouts
before any test runs. It is currently blocking changes across multiple concurrent sessions.

## PROVEN — a homogeneous failure class

Among today's last 40 `Gerrit Verified Gate` runs, FOUR failed in the checkout step
(`require resolvable rebar ticket`). **All four carry the identical signature:**

```
run 33995047786  change 2684 PS2   7x HTTP 504 | 7x RPC failed | 2x expected 'packfile'
run 33994272323  change 2686 PS1      HTTP 504 | RPC failed    | expected 'packfile'
run 33975450189  change 2680 PS1      HTTP 504 | RPC failed    | expected 'packfile'
run 33975439688  change 2666 PS9      HTTP 504 | RPC failed    | expected 'packfile'
```

4 of 4 — not a sample, the whole class. Two occurred within one hour of each other on changes
owned by DIFFERENT sessions, so this is not one session's misconfiguration.

## PROVEN — corroboration from three other vantage points, same window

- `Mirror Guard` runs 33990613226 (20:36Z) and 33991235523 (20:49Z) failed with
  `{"check":"io","healthy":false,"reason":"fetch error: <urlopen error _ssl.c:993: The handshake
  operation timed out>"}` — while the mirror was VERIFIABLY IN SYNC (Gerrit and GitHub `main` both
  at `4c9940348148`). The guard could not reach the host; nothing had diverged.
- A `curl` to the Gerrit REST API from a developer host returned an empty body with no HTTP code,
  and succeeded on immediate retry.
- A `git fetch` from the `gerrit` remote returned HTTP 504 and succeeded on retry.

Five independent observations, four distinct clients (GitHub Actions runner, GitHub Actions
checkout action, developer curl, developer git), one host.

## CORRECTION to an earlier framing — do not repeat it

`Gerrit Verified Gate` shows 20 of 36 completed runs failing today (55%), which looks like a
catastrophic gate. **It is NOT all this bug.** Partitioned by failing job:

```
optionality (lean-runtime + packaging)   10   the terraform-config-inspect canary bug,
                                              root-caused and FIXED earlier today (2678/2676/2677)
require resolvable rebar ticket           4   THIS BUG
build-and-test                            5   includes one CANCELLATION (2683 PS2, superseded)
                                              and genuine test failures
verify-identity                           1   one-off
```

The headline 55% is dominated by an already-fixed defect. Anyone citing it as evidence for this
bug is over-attributing — I nearly did.

## HYPOTHESIS — a LEAD, explicitly NOT established

A 504 on a git fetch is a gateway timeout waiting for Gerrit to produce a packfile, which is
CPU- and IO-intensive. The same host is under known IO pressure:

- `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` holds 9.3 GB on the ROOT filesystem because the dedicated EBS
  volume was never formatted or mounted (`renowned-corked-hapuku` / dcc3), so review-gate snapshots
  and per-review clones contend with the OS disk — the exact outage shape of bug 3276.
- The observability probe is being SIGTERM-ed on its 4-minute timeout with only ~42 s of CPU
  consumed, i.e. it is blocked on I/O (`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` / 9313), and its tail metrics
  have degraded to roughly 1 datapoint in 3 hours.

So "IO saturation slows packfile generation past the proxy timeout" is PLAUSIBLE and would link
three open tickets. It is NOT proven: no correlation has been established between 504 timestamps
and host IO, and no proxy timeout value has been read. Do not fix on the strength of this
paragraph — test it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 A falsifiable hypothesis for the 504s is stated, with the observation that would
      disprove it, BEFORE any fix.
- [ ] AC2 The mechanism is established by correlating 504 timestamps against host-side evidence
      (Gerrit/httpd logs, proxy timeout configuration, host IO and CPU at those instants) — not by
      plausibility. The IO hypothesis above must be confirmed or refuted explicitly.
- [ ] AC3 If the cause is a proxy/gateway timeout that is simply too short for legitimate packfile
      work, say so — raising it is then a fix, not a workaround. If instead the host cannot serve
      in reasonable time, that is a capacity finding and needs a different remedy. Distinguish
      them.
- [ ] AC4 CI distinguishes a transport failure from a test verdict, so a 504 checkout does not
      present as a change's failure. It currently reads as the change being broken; four changes
      across three sessions were mislabelled today.
- [ ] AC5 A measurable before/after rate is recorded, using the PARTITIONED counts above rather
      than the raw 55%.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (exit 127) —
bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Terraform may be written and validated; applying is
operator-authorized this session and must follow a reviewed plan. Do not touch the shared main
checkout; do not `git stash` anywhere.
compiled_state.title: Gerrit returns HTTP 504 on git fetch, breaking CI checkouts across sessions
